summary: Jacques Giès (1950–2021) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and Beaux-Arts de Paris, and served as Chief Curator of Chinese Painting at the Musée Guimet from circa 1980 to 2008.

Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1968–1981) and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1992).

Jacques P. Leider (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1987–1998) and served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques Scheuer (born 1942) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, later holding posts at Facultés Loyola Paris and Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, Kolkata (~1887–1892), and later held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1926–1928).
Jae-seong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Yasunori Ejima.

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1929–1931) and the University of Kelaniya (~1933–1935), and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Marlboro College, University of Hawaii, and CUNY Graduate Center, he held posts at City College of New York, NYU, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and Brown University (attested 2013–2018).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Marburg (~1925–1927) and University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., holding posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State, and McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff (born 1937) is a linguist. He studied at Harvard University (~1954–1959) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967), where he subsequently held a post from circa 1970 to 2006.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Atkinson (1780–1852) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1798–1802) and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate and doctoral studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where his teachers included Geshe Lhundub Sopa and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess (1832–1916) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He founded The Indian Antiquary (1872) and Epigraphia Indica (1892), succeeded Alexander Cunningham in 1885, and served multiple times as head of the Archaeological Survey of India.

James Burnell Robinson (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1967–1975) under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later teaching at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).

James C. Dobbins works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University by 1984 and held the position of Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indology scholar. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and later served as professor of law at Presidency University, Kolkata.
James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa.
